title: First Users
summary: The first 10 users are teachers, not just numbers — Feedback Loop is more effective than ads.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Why the first 10 users teach you reality — more than any plan on paper.
- Why now? The app is live — but the silence is concerning. You need real people to try it and tell the truth.
- What after the lesson? You will write an invitation message + two questions to ask after the experience.

sections.heading: Tension — Live — No One Is Using It
sections.subtitle: Live — No One Is Using It
sections.contentMarkdown:
- The link works. Technically, everything is fine. But there are no sign-ups — no feedback.
- You post on Facebook and wait. 500 visitors, 20 sign up, and no one returns.
- The problem is not marketing — the problem is that you don't hear from 10 people you know by name.

sections.heading: Core Idea — The First 10 Users Teach You Reality
sections.subtitle: The First 10 Users Teach You Reality
sections.contentMarkdown:
- The first 10 are not for numbers — they are for learning. They ask: Does this solve a problem? Or is it just a pretty design?
- 5–10 people you know + a 15-minute call each week is better than 1000 visitors from an ad.
- Iteration: You listen → fix one problem → go back to them. After a month — the product is what people need.

sections.heading: Comparison — Waiting for Visitors vs Listening to 10 People
sections.subtitle: Waiting for Visitors vs Listening to 10 People
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Launch and Wait | 10 Early Users + Listening |
|--------------|-------------------|
| Public post → Visitors → Sign-ups → No return. You add features without knowing what people need | 10 people by name. Three calls each week: “Why did you last open it?” “What could you not do?”. One problem → fix it → return |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms to Start
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Early Adopters | Those who try the product before it is complete — and tolerate the issues | Your friends try your restaurant on the first day when the lighting is not set up yet |
| Feedback Loop | You listen → adjust → go back to the user → listen again. The fastest way to improve | “The problem you mentioned is fixed” — and you go back to get their opinion |

sections.heading: Screenshot Block (Intent)
sections.contentMarkdown: Measuring Progress — Not Just for Looks: When building your app interface — think: How does the user see their progress? These numbers drive behavior — not just for decoration.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: After 4 weeks: 4 out of 10 are still using the app. What is the right decision?
Go back and talk to those who left and those who stayed — understand the problem before new marketing.
Start ads to bring in 10 more.
Give up — the product has failed.
Explanation: 40% retention needs understanding — not just new numbers. Listen first, then decide.

sections.heading: Mission — Invitation Message + 2 Questions
sections.subtitle: Invitation Message + 2 Questions
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The first 10 come from your personal effort — not from ads. 10–15 minutes. Submission: Your app in one line, invitation message for 3 people, Question 1 after the experience, Question 2 after the experience. Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clear Message | 50% | A short message — that states what the app is and asks for a specific trial; no extra marketing talk |
| Useful Questions | 50% | Two questions that elicit real feedback — not just “Did you like it?”; about actual behavior (last use, where they got stuck) |
